translationRepairs: In the first year of Kaiping under the Liang, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.
In the first year of Kaiping under the Liang, he was given the additional titles of Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant.
檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant; Grand Guardian would translate 太保, a different office.
In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.
In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, he was given the additional titles of Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant.
The literal field contains the same confusion of 太尉 with 太保.
Yan, who had originally borne the name Yan, was Qian’s son by a concubine.
Yan, whose original name was a homophonous Yan written with a different character, was Qian's son by a concubine.
The source distinguishes the later name from the original homophone. This wording makes the renaming intelligible without inserting Chinese characters into the English field.
He also contended westward with Ma Yin over Rong and Gui; Yin took the Gui circuit and captured Shizheng;
He also contended westward with Ma Yin over Rong and Gui; Ma Yin took the Gui circuit and captured Shizheng;
Repeating Ma Yin's full name resolves the otherwise misleading bare 'Yin,' which can be read as the chapter's main subject Liu Yin.
Kezhen also attacked and took the capital of Jiaozhi, plundered its treasures, and returned.
Kezhen also attacked Champa, plundered its treasures, and returned.
占城 is Champa, not the capital of Jiaozhi. The revision corrects the place without inserting Chinese characters into the English field.
Yan’s original name was Yan; he later changed it to Zhi.
Yan's original name was a homophonous Yan written with a different character; he later changed it to Zhi.
The English needs to convey that the first two names are written differently despite sharing a pronunciation; the proposed Chinese annotations are not appropriate inside the English field.
